description: Na₂Ge₂O₅ crystallizes in the orthorhombic Pna2₁ space group. There are two inequivalent Na sites. In the first Na site, Na is bonded to five O atoms to form distorted NaO₅ square pyramids that share corners with four equivalent NaO₅ square pyramids, corners with four GeO₄ tetrahedra, and  an edgeedge with one GeO₄ tetrahedra. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.37-2.60 Å. In the second Na site, Na is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to six O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.30-2.73 Å. There are two inequivalent Ge sites. In the first Ge site, Ge is bonded to four O atoms to form GeO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with two equivalent NaO₅ square pyramids, corners with three GeO₄ tetrahedra, and  an edgeedge with one NaO₅ square pyramid. There are a spread of Ge-O bond distances ranging from 1.70-1.79 Å. In the second Ge site, Ge is bonded to four O atoms to form GeO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with two equivalent NaO₅ square pyramids and corners with three GeO₄ tetrahedra. There are a spread of Ge-O bond distances ranging from 1.71-1.79 Å. There are five inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded to four Na and one Ge atom to form a mixture of distorted corner and edge-sharing ONa₄Ge trigonal bipyramids. In the second O site, O is bonded in a distorted trigonal planar geometry to one Na and two equivalent Ge atoms. In the third O site, O is bonded in a distorted trigonal planar geometry to one Na and two equivalent Ge atoms. In the fourth O site, O is bonded to four Na and one Ge atom to form a mixture of distorted corner and edge-sharing ONa₄Ge trigonal bipyramids. In the fifth O site, O is bonded in a distorted bent 120 degrees geometry to one Na and two Ge atoms.
